**The fix:** in `site/css/styles.css`, the shared heading rule (`h1`–`h6`) had `margin-bottom: 0.75rem`. Bootstrap's default is `0.5rem`. That pushed everything under each heading down by 4px, and the phone page came out 4px taller. I set it back to `0.5rem`. Page heights now match the approved screenshots at desktop and phone size, and every element sits in the same position as before.

**What still differs:** `npx playwright test tests/visual.spec.ts` still fails on both sizes, with about 2% of pixels different. Those pixels are only inside text, mainly slightly different letter spacing. That includes the "900×400" text inside the placeholder SVG image. Page CSS can't change that text, so I think the cause is how fonts render in this environment, such as the Inter font files or text hinting, and not the site.

I tried the obvious CSS knobs: kerning, `text-rendering`, letter and word spacing, font weight, font size, and font family. None of them improved the match, so I reverted all of them. The only change left is the margin fix.

**Your call:** if the approved screenshots were made on a machine with different font rendering, you'll need to regenerate them. Otherwise the test will keep failing on text. I haven't updated the snapshots, since that would replace your approved baselines.
